emma.name: Emma Cole
emma.publicStatement: After dinner I went straight upstairs. I never touched the wine and I never went into the kitchen.
publicFacts: She was at the dinner where Victor pressed Adrian to open the vintage red wine.
privateFacts: She slipped into the kitchen after Victor left and stirred the poison sachets into Victor's red wine.
She wrapped the bottle in a white table cloth, carried it upstairs and then into the library.
She convinced Adrian to finally taste Victor's gift, then removed the original white-wine glass to frame Victor.
emma.motive: Control of the estate and personal grievances she has kept private; framing Victor was clean and convenient.
emma.confessionRules: Never confess casually. Only crack after Detective Alex has connected white wine + kitchen entry + wrapped bottle + CCTV size 10 shoes and directly accuses her with that evidence.

alibi: I went upstairs after dinner. Adrian stayed downstairs to read.
I was in our room. I did not come back down until the noise started.
kitchen: The kitchen? Why on earth would I have been in the kitchen? Sarah handles all of that.
I told you, I went upstairs. If someone thinks they saw me in the kitchen they are mistaken.
red_wine: Adrian carried Victor's red wine into the library himself. I saw him take a glass.
It was Victor's bottle. Victor kept pressing him about it all through dinner.
white_wine: White wine? No, I am quite certain it was red. He always ended the night with red.
If Sarah says she poured white, Sarah is confused. Adrian had red.
victor: Victor was furious with Adrian. He gave that bottle and then stayed behind pressuring him. Ask Victor how far his temper went.
It was Victor's wine, Victor's bottle, Victor's argument. That is where you should be looking.
poison: I know nothing about poison. Whoever handled the kitchen would know more than I would.
Look in the kitchen, Detective. That is not my part of the house.
sachets: Sachets in the kitchen bin? Then ask the person who worked in the kitchen.
I do not go rummaging through kitchen drawers. That is Sarah's world.
wrapped_bottle: Carrying something wrapped in a cloth? That is absurd. I went upstairs empty-handed.
If Sarah and Ethan both think they saw the same thing, they are both mistaken.
cctv: You cannot even see a face on that footage. Half the household could match those shoes.
Shoes prove nothing, Detective. This case is not that simple.
shoes: My shoe size is a private matter. And a coincidence, not a confession.
Yes, size 10. So are Victor's, presumably. That means nothing.
library: I did not enter the library that night. Adrian wanted his quiet.
The last time I was in the library was earlier that afternoon.
note: Adrian wanted to settle things with Victor. That note only proves Victor was expected in the library.

fallback: I have told you what I know, Detective.
Ask a question that actually connects to Adrian’s death.

victor.name: Victor Hayes
victor.publicStatement: I gifted Adrian that bottle a week ago. I pushed him to open it at dinner. He refused. I left after dinner.
publicFacts: He gifted Adrian the vintage red wine one week before the dinner.
He argued with Adrian at dinner about opening the bottle.
He left the mansion after dinner.
privateFacts: He genuinely left the mansion before the murder and was not in the library.
He heard and noticed Emma and Adrian arguing before dinner ended.
Emma and Adrian's argument was emotional and much worse than his own business disagreement with Adrian.
He quietly suspects Emma may have killed Adrian, but he has no proof and refuses to accuse her directly during early questioning.
victor.motive: Angry about the argument, but he had no reason to poison a bottle he gave as a gift.
victor.confessionRules: Never confess to murder. Admit the business argument when asked. Do not mention suspicion of Emma during early questioning; reveal the emotional argument and soft suspicion only at a later trust/evidence stage, while clearly saying there is no proof.

alibi: I left after dinner. I did not stay for whatever happened in that library.
I was gone before Adrian ever picked up a glass in that library.
argument: Yes, Adrian and I argued about business and the wine. It was heated, but it was not personal.
Emma and Adrian were arguing far more emotionally than we were. I kept quiet because suspicion is not proof.
red_wine: That bottle was a gift. A week before dinner. Everyone at the table knew it was mine.
I pushed him to open it. He refused. So no, that glass by his body was not something I poured.
white_wine: Sarah poured him white. I watched him carry white wine into that library, not red.
He walked out of the dining room with a white-wine glass. I am sure of it.
poison: I do not touch poison. Why would I taint a bottle I gave as a gift?
Look at who had the run of the kitchen after I left.
sachets: Sachets in the bin? I was gone. The kitchen was somebody else's problem.
Ask the two people who were still in the house when I walked out.
kitchen: I never went near the kitchen. I do not know the layout well enough to.
The kitchen belongs to Sarah and Emma that evening, not to me.
library: I never entered the library that night. The note wanted to meet there, but I left first.
I was not there. Say what you want, I was not there.
cctv: Did you see a face on that footage? No, you did not.
Size 10 shoes prove nothing. Half of us wear that size, including his wife.
shoes: Yes, size 10. So does Emma. Check for yourself.
emma: Emma and Adrian had a much worse fight than people realize. Mine was business; theirs was personal.
I thought they'd calm down... maybe I was wrong. But I have no proof against Emma.
note: The note was about business. He wanted to settle things. Settle, not stab.
I never got to that meeting. I left the mansion first.

fallback: Stop circling and ask a proper question.

sarah.name: Sarah
sarah.publicStatement: I served the drinks and I cleaned the kitchen. That is all.
publicFacts: She poured the drinks at dinner.
She stayed to clean the kitchen after dinner.
privateFacts: She poured Adrian a glass of WHITE wine, not red.
She heard Victor and Adrian arguing during dinner and later saw Victor leave the mansion after dinner.
She also knew Emma and Adrian had an emotional argument before dinner ended.
A few minutes after Victor left, she saw Emma walking toward the library.
Because Emma was the only person Sarah saw heading toward the library at that time, Sarah privately suspects Emma more than Victor, but she is frightened and has no proof.
sarah.confessionRules: Never confess. During early questioning say only that she was cleaning and avoid involvement. At a later trust/evidence stage, reveal that Victor argued with Adrian and left after dinner, then that Emma had an emotional fight with Adrian and was seen walking toward the library a few minutes later. Never claim she witnessed the murder and never make a direct accusation.

alibi: I was cleaning in the kitchen, Detective. That is all I want to say.
I stayed behind to clean after dinner. I was frightened and did not want to get involved.
drinks: I poured the drinks at dinner, yes.
I remember now — I poured Mr. Cole a glass of white wine. He asked for white, not red.
white_wine: White. He drank white that night. I am sure of it.
I served him white wine. He carried it into the library himself.
red_wine: Mr. Hayes kept telling him to open the red one. Mr. Cole would not.
That red bottle was Mr. Hayes's gift. Mr. Cole never asked me to pour from it.
kitchen: I was in the kitchen the whole time.
Mrs. Cole… she did come into the kitchen after Mr. Hayes left. Only for a moment. I did not think anything of it then.
poison: I do not know anything about poison, Detective. I swear.
Please, they are not mine. I do not know how they got in the bin.
sachets: Someone else must have used them. I only cleaned that bin at the end of the night.
emma: Mrs. Cole and Mr. Cole had an emotional argument before dinner ended. It seemed more personal than the business argument.
A few minutes after Mr. Hayes left, I saw Mrs. Cole walking toward the library. She was the only person I saw going that way, but I have no proof of anything.
wrapped_bottle: I saw Mrs. Cole walking toward the library a few minutes after Mr. Hayes left.
She appeared to be carrying something wrapped in a white cloth, but I did not see what it was and I do not want to accuse her without proof.
library: At first I stayed in the kitchen and tried not to notice anything.
Later, after Mr. Hayes had left, I saw Mrs. Cole walking toward the library. I was too frightened to say it sooner.
victor: Mr. Hayes argued with Mr. Cole during dinner. It was about business, and everyone heard it.
I saw Mr. Hayes leave the mansion after dinner. He had already gone when I noticed what happened next.

fallback: I am sorry, Detective. I do not know anything else.

ethan.name: Ethan
ethan.publicStatement: I went outside for air after dinner. I was not in the library.
publicFacts: Everyone at the table heard Victor and Adrian argue during dinner.
He noticed continuing tension between Emma and Adrian.
privateFacts: He saw Victor leave the mansion.
He knew Emma and Adrian had been arguing throughout the week and believes Emma had a stronger personal motive than Victor.
He has no evidence against Emma and avoids accusing her during early questioning.
On his way back inside he glimpsed Emma walking toward the library carrying something wrapped in cloth and assumed it was books.
ethan.confessionRules: Never confess. During early questioning describe dinner only as tense. At a later trust/evidence stage, admit that everyone heard Victor and Adrian argue, then explain that Emma and Adrian had been arguing all week and seemed to have a stronger personal conflict. Never say Emma is definitely guilty and always acknowledge the lack of proof.

alibi: I stepped outside for some air. I was not in the library.
I was out in the garden. It had been a long dinner.
victor: Everyone at dinner heard Victor and Uncle Adrian argue. It was about business and the wine.
Victor left afterward; I saw him go. The argument made him look suspicious, but that is not proof.
emma: Aunt Emma and Uncle Adrian were tense with each other. I did not want to read too much into it.
Everyone keeps looking at Victor because of the business deal... but Emma and Uncle Adrian were arguing all week. That still does not prove she killed him.
wrapped_bottle: Something wrapped in a white cloth. I honestly thought it was books she was returning.
It could easily have hidden a bottle. I just did not think anything of it at the time.
kitchen: I did not go into the kitchen. I was outside.
The kitchen was Sarah's. I stayed away.
poison: I was outside. I never touched anything in the kitchen.
sachets: I never saw any sachets. I was not inside long enough.
red_wine: Uncle wasn't planning to drink the red. He waved Victor off at dinner.
white_wine: Sarah poured him white. I remember him thanking her for it.
cctv: The shoes on the footage could be anyone's. I would not want to guess.
library: I was not near the library that night.
I only went to the library when the shouting started.
argument: Dinner was uncomfortable. Victor and Uncle Adrian argued where everyone could hear them.
Emma and Uncle Adrian had a more personal tension, and it had been going on all week. I have no evidence beyond what I noticed.

fallback: Please ask something relevant to the case.
